content.title: Michigan Wolverines finish undefeated season with national title
content.text: Michigan Wolverines head coach Jim Harbaugh hugs running back Blake Corum (2) after his 12-yard touchdown put the Wolverines up 27-13 during the national championship NCAA College Football Playoff game at NRG Stadium, Monday, Jan. 8, 2024, in Houston.Brett Coomer/Staff photographerRains hit Houston so hard on Monday night NRG Stadium briefly had a rare leaky roof covering college football’s brightest stage. A smidgen later Michigan, in finest Southeast Texas gully-washer fashion, hit Washington so hard the Huskies sprang a leak they could not ultimately plug in the College Football Playoff national title game.As storms slowly rolled out of Houston, Michigan’s early torrent beneath NRG’s roof, primarily courtesy of a lightning-quick running back, in the end lifted the Wolverines to a 34-13 victory and their first national title in 26 years.Article continues below this ad“We’re 15-0 and took on all-comers, we’re the last one standing,” a triumphant Michigan coach Jim Harbaugh said.The dud in terms of any late drama followed two of the best CFP semifinal games in its 10-season history: a 27-20 Michigan win over Alabama in overtime in the Rose Bowl and a 37-31 Washington win over Texas in the Sugar Bowl, both on New Year’s Day.The Wolverines rolled from Pasadena, Calif., to within a Donovan Edwards breakaway sprint of Pasadena, Texas, with hardly a stagger in winning their first national title since 1997. Michigan won its first outright national championship since 1948, while Washington failed to win its first title since 1991.Washington (14-1) perhaps figured things wouldn’t go its way in its first CFP title game appearance when Michigan’s Edwards had 87 yards on his first two carries — and most importantly for the Wolverines’ fortunes two touchdown runs of 41 and 46 yards to stake Michigan to a 14-3 lead with more than two minutes remaining in the first quarter.Article continues below this adMichigan running back Blake Corum finished with 134 rushing yards, including the game’s final two touchdowns, and Edwards wound up with 104 rushing yards, the first time a team has had two 100-yard rushers in a CFP title game.The Wolverines are the second consecutive team to finish 15-0, following Georgia a year ago. Five of the last six national champions have finished undefeated, with the lone “blemish” Georgia’s 14-1 mark in 2021.The Wolverines last played a bowl game in Texas in December 1995, a 22-20 loss to Texas A&M in the Alamo Bowl in San Antonio. Suffice to say Wolverines fans will cherish their trek just a bit inside Loop 610 much more than that River Walk jaunt from nearly 30 years ago.Harbaugh, in his ninth season leading the charge of his alma mater, said he’s preached togetherness from the time of his arrival to Ann Arbor, Mich., in 2015. Harbaugh, a San Francisco 49ers coach from 2011-14, won his first championship in either the NFL or college.Article continues below this ad“The perfect fighting unit to me is a pack of wolves — a wolfpack,” Harbaugh said in the days leading to the title tussle. “You see them gathered together before the fight, and you see them celebrating after the fight. The active word there is ‘together.’”Following their quick start, the Wolverines settled in and didn’t score another touchdown until midway through the fourth quarter, when Corum broke a tackle to scoot into the end zone from 12 yards.The touchdown shoved the Wolverines to a 27-13 lead with 7:09 remaining. Michigan returned to a more up-tempo approach on the possession, a 71-yard drive fueled by a 41-yard completion over the middle by quarterback J.J. McCarthy to tight end Colston Loveland.Article continues below this adMichigan sports the nation’s top scoring defense, and Washington’s typically potent passing game repeatedly missed the mark behind strong-armed quarterback Michael Penix Jr., who finished second in the Heisman Trophy race to LSU quarterback Jayden Daniels.Penix, consistently under pressure from Michigan’s rousing defensive front seven, finished 27 of 51 for 255 yards with half as many touchdown passes (one) as interceptions (two). Penix on a fourth down and 13 late in the game heaved a desperation pass that Michigan defensive back Mike Sainristil intercepted and returned 81 yards before he was tackled 8 yards shy of a touchdown.Two plays later Corum punched in a touchdown, and the party was on among the blue and maize bunch. The Wolverines won the college title in the same building former Michigan quarterback Tom Brady won two Super Bowls with the New England Patriots in 2004 and 2017.The Wolverines overcame constant scuttlebutt that Harbaugh might head back to the NFL after the season, and an NCAA investigation into possible recruiting violations and a sign-stealing scandal.Article continues below this adHarbaugh received separate three-game suspensions to start the regular season and end the regular season because of the allegations, and the six games meant he missed half the regular season.The inspirational leader was around for the games that mattered most, however, the Wolverines’ shutout of Iowa in the Big Ten title game and the consecutive CFP victories against Alabama of the SEC and Washington of the Pac-12.The Huskies are exiting the Pac-12 for the Big Ten this summer, and the teams are scheduled to meet on Oct. 5 in Seattle in a conference contest — one much less hyped than the 10th CFP title game.Article continues below this adJan 8, 2024Former Texas A&M Beat WriterBrent Zwerneman is a former staff writer for the Houston Chronicle who covered Texas A&M athletics. He is a graduate of Oak Ridge High School and Sam Houston State University, where he played baseball. Brent is the author of four published books about Texas A&M, three related to A&M athletics. He’s a seven-time winner of APSE National Top 10 writing awards for the Houston Chronicle and San Antonio Express-News, including in 2021 breaking the bombshell college football story of the decade: Texas and Oklahoma secretly planning a move to the SEC. He netted a national APSE second-place finish for breaking the Dennis Franchione “secret newsletter” scandal in 2007, and his coverage of Texas A&M’s move to the SEC from the Big 12 also netted a third-place finish nationally in 2012. Brent was named national beat writer of the year by the Football Writers Association of America for 2021, the first Texan to earn the honor, but he’s most proud on the sports front of earning Dayton Invitational Basketball Tournament MVP honors in 1988. Brent met his wife, KBTX-TV news anchor Crystal Galny, in the Dixie Chicken before an A&M-Texas Tech football game in 2002, and the couple has three children: Will, Zoe and Brady.
